Title: Dietary Supplementation on Physical Performance and Recovery in Active-Duty Military Personnel: A Systematic Review of Randomized and Quasi-Experimental Controlled Trials.
Exact_Result: Sixteen studies reported inconsistent and mostly modest performance/recovery findings; authors state there is inadequate practical evidence for field performance guidance.
Study_Design: Systematic review of randomized and quasi-experimental controlled trials

Title: The Effects of Protein and Carbohydrate Supplementation, with and without Creatine, on Occupational Performance in Firefighters.
Exact_Result: Creatine group showed larger improvement in rescue (difference 1.78 s, 95% CI 0.61-2.95; p=.004) and forcible entry (2.66 s, 95% CI 0.68-4.65; p=.01), with no interaction for other tasks or total time.

Title: Graduation-stage physical fitness as a predictor of operational performance and injury risk among police recruits: a prospective cohort study.
Source_Locator: Results Table 1 and multivariable regression results; Limitations.
Exact_Result: Among 216 followed recruits, each one-point composite fitness increase was associated with HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.83-0.95) for injury; BARS association beta=0.21 (95% CI 0.12-0.30).
Population: 216 followed recruits at one Chinese police academy

Title: The reliability, validity and usefulness of the 30-15 intermittent fitness test for cardiorespiratory fitness assessment in military personnel.
Exact_Result: End-running speed, maximal heart rate and predicted VO2max test-retest ICCs were .971, .960 and .975; authors report validity/usefulness against treadmill and 2-mile run measures.
